slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
Volume of a sphere: V = (4/3)πr3.

Compare a hemisphere of radius r with a cylinder of radius r and height r that has a cone (apex down) removed. At height y, the hemisphere's cross section is a circle of area π(r2 − y2), and the cylinder-minus-cone's is a ring of area πr2 − πy2. Equal at every height, so by Cavalieri the volumes are equal: πr3 − (1/3)πr3 = (2/3)πr3. Double for the sphere.

Archimedes was so proud of the sphere and cylinder that he asked for them on his tombstone.
